tasks.short: Explain the day's work to helpers, show cutting and preassembly, check their work and give them cut lists.

steps.what: Plumber explains the day's work to helpers on site
Plumber writes cut lists for helpers: on paper today; after the change the calculator's cut lengths form the list
Plumber checks the cut list: lengths, diameters and quantities match the installation plan
Plumber shares the checked cut list to the helpers' phones
Plumber directs helpers engaged in pipe cutting and preassembly
Plumber checks the helpers' work

tasks.design: Cut lengths entered in the pipe calculator on the tablet ({OTHER}) become a cut list that the plumber checks and shares to the helpers' phones, instead of a paper list. Briefing, directing and checking the helpers stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cut lists were written by hand on site.
tasks.enabler_now: Pipe calculator apps share cut lists.
tasks.still_hard: Helpers learn by watching; a list does not replace showing.
tasks.human_edge: Teaching a new helper to deburr every cut without being told.

reach.learn: Whether shared cut lists cut mistakes.

evidence.claim: Pipe calculator apps produce and share cut lists.

assumptions: Boundary: from the plan to checked work; installation is outside.
Input contract: installation plan made by the plumber; fallback is paper.
Briefing, directing, checking the helpers' work and checking and sharing the list keep their full time. s2 keeps 40 for adding items the calculator does not cover.

incremental.description: No upkeep: sharing the list is step s2s.

approvals.approved_version: The cut list with lengths, diameters and quantities exactly as checked by the plumber in s2c, shared once with the helpers on this job in the app; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many cut lengths are not in the calculator, so lists are mostly written by hand (2.6); high: lengths come from the calculator (7.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Visit the site, count materials and price them, estimate labour hours, pass the estimate into the project plan and discuss it.

steps.what: Plumber visits the site and notes the work
Plumber counts materials and looks up their prices
Plumber estimates labor hours for each part of the work
Plumber checks the finished calculation: quantities, prices and hours fit the work noted on site
The estimate goes into the project plan: typed into the planning sheet by the plumber today, fed from the calculation after the change
Plumber discusses the estimate with the project manager

tasks.design: The calculation module of the installer's ERP ({ERP}) prices materials from the sector's product and price data and proposes labour hours from the firm's norm times per activity; the plumber adjusts quantities and hours. The plumber checks the finished calculation, which then feeds the project plan directly. The site visit and the talk with the project manager stay with the plumber.
tasks.previous_blocker: Estimates were built in spreadsheets with prices looked up by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Installer ERPs combine sector price data and norm times in calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Norm times miss old buildings and awkward access; the plumber's judgement corrects them.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing in a crawl space that the job will take twice as long.
tasks.altitude: The plumber adjusts calculated estimates instead of building them.

reach.learn: Whether calculated estimates are closer to actual hours.

evidence.claim: 2BA is a product and price data hub for the Dutch installation sector that installer software connects to.
Syntess Atrium captures work orders, hours and materials for installation firms.

assumptions: Boundary: from the site visit to the agreed estimate; client quotes are outside.
Input contract: norm times per activity kept by the firm's calculator; prices from the sector data hub; fallback is the spreadsheet.
The site visit, the talk and the calculation check keep their full time. s2 keeps 40 because quantities are still counted and adjusted. s3 keeps 60 for adjusting proposed hours.
Project manager time is outside the plumber's savings.
research_questions: Do actual hours come closer to estimated hours?

already_counted.description: Plumber adjusts calculated quantities and hours.

incremental.description: No focal upkeep: the firm's calculator keeps the norm times and the sector hub the prices.

approvals.approved_version: The calculation with quantities, prices and hours exactly as checked by the plumber in s3c, fed once into this project's plan in the {ERP}; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual jobs where norms fit badly and many items need manual prices (23.5); high: standard jobs (37.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Get the next job, record hours and materials, get the client's signature, attach photos, hand in work orders and note what was done.

steps.what: Plumber phones the office for the next job and its details
Plumber records hours worked and materials used: on the paper work order today; with hours typed and materials scanned or picked in the app after the change
Plumber writes a note on what was done

loop.input: The plumber's voice note at the end of the job and the job checklist.
loop.output: Filled checklist fields and a short draft remark.
loop.check: Code validates fields against the job checklist and requires a photo for every item that will be closed in. The plumber reads each field and the remark against what was done and the photos, removes anything not said, and types what the draft missed.
loop.stop: One draft per job; on failure the plumber fills the checklist by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fitters speak freely at the end of a job; a form alone takes longer to fill on a phone.

steps.what: Plumber sends photos of the work by chat to the office
Plumber gets the client's signature on the paper work order
Client signs the work order on the plumber's phone
Plumber checks the signed work order before it goes to the office: hours, materials, note and photos match the job, and the client's signature is there
The signed work order goes into the ERP: dropped at the office for typing today, posted from the phone after the change

tasks.design: Jobs reach the plumber's phone as digital work orders from the planning board in the installer's ERP ({ERP}), so no call is needed for the next job. Hours and materials are entered with pick lists and scans, photos attach to the job, and a voice note becomes checklist fields and a remark that the plumber confirms. The client signs on the phone, the plumber checks the signed order, and it then lands in the ERP without typing. No location tracking is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Jobs came by phone and paper work orders were retyped by the office.
tasks.enabler_now: Installer ERPs send work orders to phones and take hours, materials, photos and signatures.
tasks.still_hard: Dead spots and dirty hands; the app must work offline and with gloves.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining to a client what was done and why it took longer.

reach.learn: Whether digital work orders shorten time to invoice.

evidence.claim: A sewer cleaning firm replaced paper work orders with about 200 handhelds; orders per day rose from 1,500-1,600 to about 2,000 and the investment paid back in six months (director's figures, 2009).
Syntess Atrium captures work orders, hours and materials on site.
Hours, location and job logs per fitter observe presence and performance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from job assignment to the order in the ERP; invoicing is outside.
Input contract: planned jobs from the office planner; checklists per job type set by the office; fallback is phone and paper.

Talking with the client and the work order check keep their full time. s1 keeps 10 for jobs whose details are incomplete. s2 keeps 80 because hours are still entered; only writing article details goes. s3 keeps 70 because the voice note replaces writing but every field and the remark are read. The client's signature (s5k, share 1) is customer time.
Office time is outside the plumber's savings.
unknowns: Whether the works council agrees to job logs.
research_questions: Does time on the phone between jobs fall?

incremental.description: Plumber syncs the app when back in coverage.

approvals.approved_version: The signed work order with hours, materials, note and photos exactly as checked by the plumber in s5c, posted once to the {ERP} for this job; any change reopens the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: poor mobile coverage and incomplete job details, so the plumber still phones for many jobs and half the orders go on paper (37.4); high: digital orders work for most jobs (50.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The plumber keeps the work, the helpers and the client; phone calls for jobs, paper orders and spreadsheet estimates shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A plumber who finishes the paperwork in the van before driving to the next job.
